threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's normal to pay for a pint with cash. Everyone else has their phones out, and you're staring at the bar like it’s an alien technology.
Last night on the 59, a guy serenaded the whole bus with a karaoke version of 'Wonderwall'. Most were tired but he got a round of applause at the end.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The sound of the U-Bahn rumbling under my feet while I sip coffee at my favorite Kreuzkölln café – that’s when I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a late-night kebab stand that doubles as a dance floor after midnight—local DJs spinning while you munch on döner.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they grab a burrito from La Taqueria and actually take the time to squeeze lime on it, even in a rush.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a dog casually taking a nap on the tracks at Civic Center. Only in SF does a fuzzy friend hold up the Muni schedule.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals eat late, but honestly, you’ll find most Gràcia families at home by 10. They just don’t rave about dinner as much.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their bewildered looks at the metro signage; locals just glide past without a second glance.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think Dalston Junction is the go-to station instead of the hidden gems like Hackney Central. You'll learn soon enough.
Caught a bloke on the 35 last night serenading the driver with 90s R&B. Whole bus chimed in. Only in Brixton, right? Pure magic.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy fix his bike while balancing a toddler on his hip, all while chatting up the local bakery owner. That's Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find spontaneous techno parties right on the Spree, where the sunset turns a simple boat into a dance floor.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a real local when they know the difference between Mission Street and Valencia during rush hour and can navigate without blinking.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 12 bus today; it was so late I almost had time to read a whole chapter. Only in SF does a bus delay feel like a mini vacation.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think it’s all about the Gaudí buildings, but locals know the real charm lies in the tiny squares where children play and old men sip vermut.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle with the 'tapa' ordering ritual; they ask for 'tapas' instead of just diving in like a local.
